intro: In a real discussion nobody gives you time to prepare. In this lesson you'll learn to join in naturally: buy a few seconds to think, build on what others say, weigh up pros and cons, make careful guesses, and take turns without waiting to be asked. Warm-up: should companies let people work from anywhere for a month a year?
teachingNotes: This speaking lesson builds on b1-giving-opinions: opinion + reason (I think … because …), agreeing (I agree, never *I am agree*) and polite disagreement (I see what you mean, but … / That's true, but …). Recap it in a line, don't re-teach it. The node's common error is *'I am agree with you' → 'I agree with you' (agree is a verb). The same trap appears with the new verbs here: *'It's depend' → 'It depends', *'I am suspect' → 'I suspect'. Topics: moving the office, working from anywhere, the company trip (Bali or Bandung), AI at work, online classes, KRL/MRT, kos rent, a shuttle bus from the station.

Spontaneous discussion. Buying time instead of silence or Indonesian fillers (eee…, apa ya…): That's a good question. / Let me think … / Hmm, let me see. / It's hard to say, but … / I've never really thought about it, but …. These answer a QUESTION; when someone gives an opinion, react to it (agree, build on it, or disagree politely). Building on others shows you're listening: Following on from what Rina said, … / To add to that, … / Going back to Budi's point, … / As Sari said, …. They add a point in the SAME direction; to go the other way, use the B1 polite disagreement. Treat 'what Rina said' as a phrase to remember. Indonesian trap: 'On the other hand' is often used for 'selain itu' (adding); it only means contrast (di sisi lain). For adding, say To add to that / Also / What's more.

Pros and cons: pros = advantages (kelebihan), cons = disadvantages (kekurangan). On the plus side, … / One advantage is that … / The downside is that … / On the other hand, … (contrast) / On balance, … (final view after weighing everything; a bit formal; Overall, … and All in all, … are fine in speech). It depends on + a noun (It depends on the price) or + a question word with statement order, as in B1 indirect questions (It depends on how much it costs, not *how much does it cost). Errors to correct: *It's depend, *It depend (it → depends), *depends of / from (Indonesian 'tergantung dari'), and a disadvantage after 'On the plus side'.

Speculating, from more to less sure: There's a good chance that … (kemungkinan besar), I'd imagine … (saya kira: a reasonable guess from what you know; a phrase to remember, would makes it softer; 'imagine' here doesn't mean fantasy), I suspect … (saya menduga; often about a problem; about a person it can sound like an accusation), It could be that … (bisa jadi: one possible explanation), plus might / may / could + verb from B1. For a guess about the past, keep the phrase and use the past simple (I suspect the client didn't read the email). Do NOT teach past modals (might have, must have), the third conditional, wish, participle clauses or non-defining relative clauses. At B2 these are tendencies: accept reasonable alternatives (I'd guess, I'd say, Probably, Perhaps). Suggest varying 'Maybe' (mungkin) when the learner starts every sentence with it.

Turn-taking and culture. In many Indonesian meetings people wait for the most senior person (Pak/Bu, the boss) to speak first, and juniors speak when asked: that's respect, not a weakness. In many English-speaking groups (international companies, seminars abroad, calls with overseas teams) everyone is expected to join in without being asked, a short polite interruption at a pause is normal, and silence can be read as 'no ideas' or 'I agree'. Present both respectfully: adapt to the group. Taking a turn: Can I come in here? / Sorry to interrupt, but … / Can I just add something? Inviting: What do you think, Sari? / Sari, what's your view? / We haven't heard from Dimas yet. Handing back: Sorry, go ahead. / Anyway, that's my view. What about you? Don't invite with 'Why are you so quiet?' or 'Say something!': it puts people on the spot.

When the learner practises, play a group member: react to the content first (build on it, or disagree politely as a model), sometimes invite them by name or ask a sudden question so they can buy time, then correct ONE thing (usually I am agree / It's depend / I am suspect, 'On the other hand' used for adding, or a guess stated as a fact).

keyPoints.title: Join in: buy time and build on others
keyPoints.explanation: Recap from B1: give an opinion with a reason, agree (I agree, not I am agree) and disagree politely (I see what you mean, but …). In a real discussion, don't go silent: buy a few seconds with That's a good question. / Let me think … / It's hard to say, but …. Show you're listening by building on what others said: Following on from what Rina said, … / To add to that, … / Going back to Budi's point, ….

examples.en: Hmm, it's hard to say, but I think the new schedule is better.
examples.id: Hmm, susah dibilang, tapi menurut saya jadwal baru lebih baik.

examples.en: Following on from what Sari said, the shuttle bus is often late too.
examples.id: Melanjutkan apa yang Sari bilang, bus antar-jemputnya juga sering telat.

examples.en: Going back to Budi's point, parking near the office costs a lot.
examples.id: Kembali ke poin Budi, parkir di dekat kantor mahal sekali.

id.title: Ikut bicara: mengulur waktu dan melanjutkan poin orang lain
id.explanation: Ulasan dari B1: sampaikan pendapat dengan alasan, nyatakan setuju (I agree, bukan I am agree) dan tidak setuju dengan sopan (I see what you mean, but …). Dalam diskusi sungguhan, jangan diam saja: ulur waktu beberapa detik dengan That's a good question. / Let me think … / It's hard to say, but …. Tunjukkan kamu mendengarkan dengan melanjutkan apa yang dikatakan orang lain: Following on from what Rina said, … / To add to that, … / Going back to Budi's point, ….

keyPoints.title: Weigh up pros and cons
keyPoints.explanation: Show both sides: On the plus side, … / One advantage is that … ; The downside is that … / On the other hand, … (only for contrast, not for adding). Then decide: On balance, … (after weighing everything). If the answer isn't simple, say It depends on + a thing: It depends on the price. depend is a verb: It depends, not It's depend; and depend on, not of or from.

examples.en: One advantage is that the new office is close to the MRT.
examples.id: Salah satu kelebihannya adalah kantor baru dekat dengan MRT.

examples.en: On the other hand, the rent there is much higher.
examples.id: Di sisi lain, sewa di sana jauh lebih mahal.

examples.en: On balance, I think we should stay where we are.
examples.id: Setelah menimbang semuanya, menurut saya kita sebaiknya tetap di sini.

id.title: Menimbang kelebihan dan kekurangan
id.explanation: Tunjukkan dua sisi: On the plus side, … / One advantage is that … ; The downside is that … / On the other hand, … (hanya untuk kontras, bukan untuk menambahkan). Lalu putuskan: On balance, … (setelah menimbang semuanya). Kalau jawabannya tidak sederhana, katakan It depends on + sesuatu: It depends on the price. depend adalah kata kerja: It depends, bukan It's depend; dan depend on, bukan of atau from.

keyPoints.title: Make careful guesses
keyPoints.explanation: When nobody knows for sure, show that it's a guess, not a fact. From more sure to less sure: There's a good chance that … / I'd imagine … / I suspect … / It could be that …, plus might, may and could from B1. I'd imagine is a phrase to remember (= saya kira). suspect is a verb: I suspect, not I am suspect.

examples.en: There's a good chance that the meeting will move to Thursday.
examples.id: Kemungkinan besar rapatnya akan pindah ke hari Kamis.

examples.en: I'd imagine rents are higher near the new station.
examples.id: Saya kira harga sewa lebih mahal di dekat stasiun baru.

examples.en: I suspect the printer needs a new part.
examples.id: Saya menduga printernya butuh suku cadang baru.

id.title: Menebak dengan hati-hati
id.explanation: Kalau tidak ada yang tahu pasti, tunjukkan bahwa itu tebakan, bukan fakta. Dari lebih yakin ke kurang yakin: There's a good chance that … / I'd imagine … / I suspect … / It could be that …, ditambah might, may dan could dari B1. I'd imagine adalah frasa untuk diingat (= saya kira). suspect adalah kata kerja: I suspect, bukan I am suspect.

keyPoints.title: Take turns and invite others
keyPoints.explanation: In many Indonesian meetings, people wait for the most senior person to speak first. In many English-speaking groups, everyone is expected to join in without being asked, and silence can look like 'no ideas' or 'I agree'. Take a turn at a pause: Can I come in here? / Sorry to interrupt, but …. Invite someone by name: What do you think, Sari? / We haven't heard from Dimas yet. Hand back: Sorry, go ahead.

examples.en: Sari, what's your view on this?
Sorry to interrupt, but can I add something about the budget?
examples.id: Maaf menyela, tapi boleh saya menambahkan sesuatu soal anggarannya?

examples.en: Anyway, that's just my view. What do you think, Pak Hasan?
examples.id: Yah, itu cuma pendapat saya. Bagaimana menurut Bapak, Pak Hasan?

id.title: Bergiliran bicara dan mengajak orang lain
id.explanation: Di banyak rapat di Indonesia, orang menunggu orang yang paling senior bicara dulu. Di banyak kelompok berbahasa Inggris, semua orang diharapkan ikut bicara tanpa ditanya, dan diam bisa terlihat seperti 'tidak punya ide' atau 'saya setuju'. Ambil giliran saat ada jeda: Can I come in here? / Sorry to interrupt, but …. Ajak seseorang dengan menyebut namanya: What do you think, Sari? / We haven't heard from Dimas yet. Kembalikan giliran: Sorry, go ahead.

guidedPractice.prompt: Rina says the new office is far from the station. You agree and want to add a point. Complete with one word: To ___ to that, there's no shuttle bus.
guidedPractice.hint: To add to that = menambahkan itu: it adds a point in the same direction as Rina's.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with one word: On the plus ___, a motorbike is cheap to run.
guidedPractice.hint: On the plus side = sisi positifnya: it introduces an advantage.

guidedPractice.prompt: Nobody knows for sure, but it's likely. Complete with one word: There's a good ___ that the meeting will finish late.
guidedPractice.hint: There's a good chance that … = kemungkinan besar …: you're fairly sure, but it's still a guess.

guidedPractice.prompt: You're leading a meeting. Complete the question to invite Dimas with one word: What's your ___, Dimas?
guidedPractice.hint: Use his name and an open question: What's your view / opinion, Dimas? (= bagaimana pendapatmu?)

independentPractice.prompt: You've talked about the pros and cons of flying and taking the train to Surabaya. Give your final view. Complete with one word: On ___, I think the train is the better choice.
independentPractice.hint: On balance = setelah menimbang semuanya: it gives your decision after both sides.

independentPractice.prompt: Turn this fact into a guess. Start with 'I suspect': The printer is broken again.
expected: i suspect the printer is broken again
i suspect that the printer is broken again
i suspect the printer's broken again
independentPractice.hint: suspect is a verb, so there's no am: I suspect + subject + verb.

independentPractice.prompt: You've finished your point. Hand the turn to Rina. Complete with one word: Anyway, that's my view. What ___ you, Rina?
independentPractice.hint: What about you? = kalau kamu? It gives the turn to someone else.

assessment.prompt: At a job interview in Jakarta, the manager asks a question you didn't expect: 'How will AI change our industry in the next five years?' You need a few seconds to think. Write a short phrase (2–6 words) to buy time before you answer.
acceptableAnswers: let me think for a moment
let me think for a second
that's a good question let me think
assessment.rubric: Full marks: any natural phrase that buys a few seconds (That's a good question / Let me think … / Let me see / It's hard to say). 'I don't know' = 20 (it ends your answer instead of buying time). 'Wait' or 'Wait a minute' = 50 (it works, but it sounds abrupt in an interview). 'I am think' = 30 (think is a verb: Let me think). 'Eee' or 'Apa ya' = 0.

assessment.prompt: In a seminar, Dimas says that online classes save students money. You agree and want to build on his point. Complete with one word: Following ___ from what Dimas said, students also don't have to pay for a kos near campus.
assessment.rubric: Correct: on (Following on from what Dimas said = melanjutkan apa yang Dimas bilang). 'up' = 30 (follow up means to check later: a different phrase). 'to' or 'in' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Rina has a job offer in Singapore. She weighs it up: 'On the plus side, the salary is much higher. The ___ is that I'll be far from my family.' Complete with one word.
assessment.rubric: Full marks: downside (kekurangannya), or another word for a disadvantage (disadvantage, drawback, problem, catch). 'negative' = 70 (understood, but 'The negative is that' is less natural). 'plus side' or 'advantage' = 0 (being far from family is a disadvantage, not a pro).

assessment.prompt: Your friend asks: 'Will the office trip to Puncak happen on Saturday?' Correct the mistake in this reply: It's depend on the weather.
acceptableAnswers: it all depends on the weather
assessment.rubric: Correct: It depends on the weather (depend is a verb, so no is; it → depends with -s). 'It depend on the weather' = 50 (no is, good, but it needs -s). 'It's depends on' = 40. 'It depends of / from the weather' = 50 (depend on, not of/from).

assessment.prompt: Your team sent an important email to a client a week ago, and there's still no reply. Nobody knows why. Make a careful guess. Complete with one word: It ___ be that they're on holiday.
assessment.rubric: Correct: could, might or may (It could be that … = bisa jadi: one possible reason). 'can' = 50 (for a guess about one situation now, use could / might / may). 'must' = 30 (must means you're almost certain: too sure when nobody knows). 'will' = 20.

assessment.prompt: In a meeting, Pak Hasan is talking about the new budget. You have an important point about it, and he stops for a moment. Complete the polite phrase to take your turn with one word: Can I come ___ here?
assessment.rubric: Correct: in (Can I come in here? = boleh saya ikut bicara di sini?). 'into' = 40 (come into is for entering a place). 'on' or 'to' = 0.

assessment.prompt: You're leading an online meeting. Sari hasn't said anything yet, and you'd like to hear her ideas. Write a short question (2–6 words) to invite her to speak.
acceptableAnswers: sari do you have any thoughts
what do you think about it sari
sari what do you think about it
assessment.rubric: Full marks: an open question that invites Sari (What do you think, Sari? / Sari, what's your view? / What about you, Sari?); using her name is best, but 'What do you think?' alone is fine. A yes/no question ('Sari, do you agree?') = 60 (it invites her, but she can answer just 'yes'). 'Why are you so quiet?' or 'Say something!' = 20 (it puts her on the spot). 'What are you think' = 40 (What do you think).

material.title: Joining in: buy time and build on others

blocks.text:
Quick recap from B1: you can give an opinion with a reason (*I think … because …*), agree (**I agree**, never *I am agree*) and disagree politely (*I see what you mean, but …*). A real discussion is faster: nobody waits while you prepare. Two skills help.

**1. Buy time.** When someone suddenly asks you a question, don't go silent and don't fill the gap with *eee… apa ya…*. Say a short phrase while you think:
- **That's a good question.** (*pertanyaan bagus*)
- **Let me think …** / **Let me see …** (*saya pikir dulu …*)
- **It's hard to say, but …** (*susah dibilang, tapi …*)
- **I've never really thought about it, but …** (*saya belum pernah benar-benar memikirkannya, tapi …*)
These are for a **question**. When someone gives an **opinion**, react to it instead: agree, build on it, or disagree politely.

**2. Build on what others said.** It shows you're listening, and it links your idea to the group:
- **Following on from what Rina said, …** (*melanjutkan apa yang Rina bilang, …*)
- **To add to that, …** (*menambahkan itu, …*)
- **Going back to Budi's point, …** (*kembali ke poin Budi, …*)
- **As Sari said, …** (*seperti kata Sari, …*)
They add a point in the **same direction**. To go the other way, use your B1 phrases (*That's true, but …*). Remember *what Rina said* (*apa yang Rina bilang*) as a phrase.

id.text:
Ulasan singkat dari B1: kamu sudah bisa memberi pendapat dengan alasan (*I think … because …*), menyatakan setuju (**I agree**, jangan pernah *I am agree*) dan tidak setuju dengan sopan (*I see what you mean, but …*). Diskusi sungguhan lebih cepat: tidak ada yang menunggu kamu bersiap. Dua keterampilan ini membantu.

**1. Ulur waktu.** Kalau seseorang tiba-tiba bertanya padamu, jangan diam dan jangan mengisi jeda dengan *eee… apa ya…*. Ucapkan frasa pendek sambil berpikir:
- **That's a good question.** (*pertanyaan bagus*)
- **Let me think …** / **Let me see …** (*saya pikir dulu …*)
- **It's hard to say, but …** (*susah dibilang, tapi …*)
- **I've never really thought about it, but …** (*saya belum pernah benar-benar memikirkannya, tapi …*)
Frasa ini untuk menjawab **pertanyaan**. Kalau seseorang memberi **pendapat**, tanggapi pendapatnya: setuju, lanjutkan, atau tidak setuju dengan sopan.

**2. Lanjutkan apa yang dikatakan orang lain.** Ini menunjukkan kamu mendengarkan, dan menghubungkan idemu dengan kelompok:
- **Following on from what Rina said, …** (*melanjutkan apa yang Rina bilang, …*)
- **To add to that, …** (*menambahkan itu, …*)
- **Going back to Budi's point, …** (*kembali ke poin Budi, …*)
- **As Sari said, …** (*seperti kata Sari, …*)
Semuanya menambahkan poin ke **arah yang sama**. Untuk arah sebaliknya, pakai frasa B1-mu (*That's true, but …*). Ingat *what Rina said* (*apa yang Rina bilang*) sebagai satu frasa.

rows.en: Hmm, let me see. I think a four-day week could work for our team.
rows.id: Hmm, coba saya pikir. Menurut saya empat hari kerja seminggu bisa jalan untuk tim kita.

rows.en: I've never really thought about it, but online exams sound fair to me.
rows.id: Saya belum pernah benar-benar memikirkannya, tapi ujian online kedengarannya adil bagi saya.
rows.note: honest: you're thinking as you speak

rows.en: Following on from what Rina said, the lift is always full at eight.
rows.id: Melanjutkan apa yang Rina bilang, liftnya selalu penuh jam delapan.

rows.en: As Sari said, the new app is much faster.
rows.id: Seperti kata Sari, aplikasi barunya jauh lebih cepat.

blocks.text:
Indonesian trap: **On the other hand** is NOT *selain itu*. It means *di sisi lain* and always shows a **contrast** (the other side). For adding a point in the same direction, say **To add to that, …**, **Also, …** or **What's more, …**.
- ✓ *The KRL is cheap. **To add to that**, it's fast.*
- ✗ *The KRL is cheap. On the other hand, it's fast.* (cheap and fast are both good: there's no contrast)

id.text:
Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: **On the other hand** BUKAN *selain itu*. Artinya *di sisi lain* dan selalu menunjukkan **kontras** (sisi sebaliknya). Untuk menambahkan poin ke arah yang sama, katakan **To add to that, …**, **Also, …** atau **What's more, …**.
- ✓ *The KRL is cheap. **To add to that**, it's fast.*
- ✗ *The KRL is cheap. On the other hand, it's fast.* (murah dan cepat sama-sama bagus: tidak ada kontras)

blocks.prompt: Your lecturer suddenly asks: 'Should first-year students take their exams online?' You need a moment. What's the best start?
options: Hmm, it's hard to say, but I think online exams are fine for some subjects.
blocks.explain: **It's hard to say, but …** buys a moment and then gives an answer. *I don't know* ends the discussion. *I am agree* is wrong twice: agree is a verb (no am), and the lecturer asked a question, not an opinion.

id.prompt: Dosenmu tiba-tiba bertanya: 'Should first-year students take their exams online?' Kamu butuh waktu sebentar. Mana awal yang terbaik?
id.explain: **It's hard to say, but …** mengulur waktu sebentar lalu memberi jawaban. *I don't know* mengakhiri diskusi. *I am agree* salah dua kali: agree adalah kata kerja (tanpa am), dan dosenmu bertanya, bukan memberi pendapat.

id.title: Ikut bicara: mengulur waktu dan melanjutkan poin orang lain

blocks.text:
Big decisions have two sides: **pros** (advantages, *kelebihan*) and **cons** (disadvantages, *kekurangan*). A strong answer shows both, then decides.

**Pros:**
- **On the plus side, …** (*sisi positifnya, …*): common in speech.
- **One advantage is that …** (*salah satu kelebihannya adalah …*): a bit more formal.

**Cons:**
- **The downside is that …** (*kekurangannya adalah …*)
- **On the other hand, …** (*di sisi lain, …*): turns to the opposite side.

**Decide:**
- **On balance, …** (*setelah menimbang semuanya, …*): your final view after weighing both sides. It's a bit formal; in relaxed speech people also say *Overall, …* or *All in all, …*.

**When the answer isn't simple:**
- **It depends on** + a thing: *It depends on the price.* (*tergantung harganya*)
- **It depends on** + how much / when / who + normal sentence order, like the indirect questions you learnt in B1: *It depends on when you leave* (not *when do you leave*).
- Or just **It depends.** and then explain.

id.text:
Keputusan besar punya dua sisi: **pros** (kelebihan) dan **cons** (kekurangan). Jawaban yang kuat menunjukkan keduanya, lalu memutuskan.

**Kelebihan:**
- **On the plus side, …** (*sisi positifnya, …*): umum dalam percakapan.
- **One advantage is that …** (*salah satu kelebihannya adalah …*): sedikit lebih formal.

**Kekurangan:**
- **The downside is that …** (*kekurangannya adalah …*)
- **On the other hand, …** (*di sisi lain, …*): beralih ke sisi sebaliknya.

**Memutuskan:**
- **On balance, …** (*setelah menimbang semuanya, …*): pendapat akhirmu setelah menimbang dua sisi. Agak formal; dalam percakapan santai orang juga bilang *Overall, …* atau *All in all, …*.

**Kalau jawabannya tidak sederhana:**
- **It depends on** + sesuatu: *It depends on the price.* (*tergantung harganya*)
- **It depends on** + how much / when / who + urutan kalimat biasa, seperti pertanyaan tidak langsung yang kamu pelajari di B1: *It depends on when you leave* (bukan *when do you leave*).
- Atau cukup **It depends.** lalu jelaskan.

rows.en: On the plus side, working from home saves two hours a day.
rows.id: Sisi positifnya, kerja dari rumah menghemat dua jam sehari.

rows.en: The downside is that it's harder to train new staff.
rows.id: Kekurangannya adalah lebih sulit melatih karyawan baru.

rows.en: On balance, I think two office days a week is the best plan.
rows.id: Setelah menimbang semuanya, menurut saya dua hari di kantor seminggu adalah rencana terbaik.

rows.en: It depends on the team. Some jobs need people in the office.
rows.id: Tergantung timnya. Beberapa pekerjaan butuh orang di kantor.

blocks.text:
Indonesian trap: *tergantung* feels like an adjective, so learners say `It's depend` ✗. But **depend** is a **verb** (*kata kerja*), just like **agree**:
- *I agree* (not *I am agree*) → **It depends** (not *It's depend*)
- *it* → the verb takes **-s**: *It depends*.
- **depend on**, not *depend of* or *depend from* (from *tergantung dari*).

id.text:
Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: *tergantung* terasa seperti kata sifat, jadi pelajar bilang `It's depend` ✗. Tapi **depend** adalah **kata kerja**, sama seperti **agree**:
- *I agree* (bukan *I am agree*) → **It depends** (bukan *It's depend*)
- *it* → kata kerjanya dapat **-s**: *It depends*.
- **depend on**, bukan *depend of* atau *depend from* (dari *tergantung dari*).

blocks.prompt: Budi asks: 'Is it better to take the MRT or an ojek online to Blok M?' Which reply is correct?
blocks.explain: **depend** is a verb, so there's no *is* (*It's*), and with *it* it takes **-s**: **It depends**. After it comes **on**, not *of* (that's the Indonesian *tergantung dari* trap).

id.prompt: Budi bertanya: 'Is it better to take the MRT or an ojek online to Blok M?' Balasan mana yang benar?
id.explain: **depend** adalah kata kerja, jadi tanpa *is* (*It's*), dan dengan *it* dapat **-s**: **It depends**. Setelahnya **on**, bukan *of* (itu jebakan *tergantung dari*).

blocks.text:
In discussions we often talk about things nobody knows for sure: why sales dropped, what the client wants, what will happen next year. **Speculating** (*berspekulasi*) means making a careful guess and showing that it's a guess, not a fact. Here they are from **more sure** to **less sure**:
- **There's a good chance that …** (*kemungkinan besar …*): you're fairly sure.
- **I'd imagine …** (*saya kira …*): a sensible guess from what you know. *I'd* = *I would*, which makes it softer; just remember it as a phrase. Here **imagine** doesn't mean *membayangkan* a dream: it means *I guess*.
- **I suspect …** (*saya menduga …*): you think it's true, often about a problem.
- **It could be that …** (*bisa jadi …*): one possible reason among others.
- **might / may / could** + verb (*mungkin*), from B1: *The client might be busy.*

For a guess about the past, keep the phrase and use the past simple: *I suspect the client didn't read the email.*

id.text:
Dalam diskusi kita sering membicarakan hal yang tidak diketahui pasti: kenapa penjualan turun, apa maunya klien, apa yang akan terjadi tahun depan. **Speculating** (*berspekulasi*) artinya menebak dengan hati-hati dan menunjukkan bahwa itu tebakan, bukan fakta. Ini urutannya dari **lebih yakin** ke **kurang yakin**:
- **There's a good chance that …** (*kemungkinan besar …*): kamu cukup yakin.
- **I'd imagine …** (*saya kira …*): tebakan masuk akal dari apa yang kamu tahu. *I'd* = *I would*, yang membuatnya lebih lembut; ingat saja sebagai satu frasa. Di sini **imagine** bukan *membayangkan* mimpi: artinya *saya kira*.
- **I suspect …** (*saya menduga …*): kamu rasa itu benar, sering tentang suatu masalah.
- **It could be that …** (*bisa jadi …*): salah satu kemungkinan alasan di antara yang lain.
- **might / may / could** + kata kerja (*mungkin*), dari B1: *The client might be busy.*

Untuk tebakan tentang masa lalu, pakai frasanya dan past simple: *I suspect the client didn't read the email.*

rows.en: There's a good chance that the new MRT line will open next year.
rows.id: Kemungkinan besar jalur MRT baru akan dibuka tahun depan.

rows.en: I'd imagine most students prefer morning classes.
rows.id: Saya kira kebanyakan mahasiswa lebih suka kelas pagi.

rows.en: I suspect the Wi-Fi is the real problem.
rows.id: Saya menduga Wi-Fi-nya masalah yang sebenarnya.
rows.note: you think it's true, about a problem

id.note: kamu rasa itu benar, tentang masalah

rows.en: It could be that people are saving money for Lebaran.
rows.id: Bisa jadi orang-orang sedang menabung untuk Lebaran.

blocks.text:
Two traps:
- **suspect** is a verb, like **agree**: **I suspect**, not `I am suspect` ✗.
- In Indonesian, *mungkin* can start almost every sentence. In English, starting every sentence with *Maybe* sounds unsure and repetitive: mix it with *I'd imagine*, *It could be that* and *might*.
Also be careful with **I suspect** + a person (*I suspect Budi …*): it can sound like you're accusing him (*mencurigai*). Use it for situations and problems.

id.text:
Dua jebakan:
- **suspect** adalah kata kerja, seperti **agree**: **I suspect**, bukan `I am suspect` ✗.
- Dalam bahasa Indonesia, *mungkin* bisa membuka hampir setiap kalimat. Dalam bahasa Inggris, memulai setiap kalimat dengan *Maybe* terdengar ragu dan berulang-ulang: campur dengan *I'd imagine*, *It could be that* dan *might*.
Hati-hati juga dengan **I suspect** + orang (*I suspect Budi …*): bisa terdengar seperti kamu menuduhnya (*mencurigai*). Pakai untuk situasi dan masalah.

blocks.prompt: The new café near your office is always empty. Nobody knows why. Which sentence is a careful guess, not a fact?
options: I suspect the prices are too high for office workers.
I am suspect the prices are too high.
blocks.explain: **I suspect …** shows it's your guess. *The coffee there is bad* sounds like a fact, but nobody knows. *I am suspect* is wrong: suspect is a verb, so there's no am.

id.prompt: Kafe baru dekat kantormu selalu sepi. Tidak ada yang tahu kenapa. Kalimat mana yang tebakan hati-hati, bukan fakta?
id.explain: **I suspect …** menunjukkan itu tebakanmu. *The coffee there is bad* terdengar seperti fakta, padahal tidak ada yang tahu. *I am suspect* salah: suspect adalah kata kerja, jadi tanpa am.

blocks.text:
**Turn-taking** means who speaks when. Here the culture matters as much as the words.

In many **Indonesian meetings**, people wait for the most senior person (*Pak/Bu*, the boss) to speak first, and juniors speak when they're asked. That's a sign of respect.

In many **English-speaking groups** (an international company, a seminar abroad, a call with an overseas team), the expectation is different: everyone, juniors too, is expected to **join in without being asked**, and a short, polite interruption at a pause is normal. If you stay quiet, people may think you have no ideas, or that you agree.

Neither style is better: just notice which one the group expects. You can join in and still be respectful: wait for a pause, use a soft phrase, keep your point short.

**Take a turn:**
- **Can I come in here?** (*boleh saya ikut bicara?*)
- **Sorry to interrupt, but …** (*maaf menyela, tapi …*)
- **Can I just add something?** (*boleh saya menambahkan sesuatu?*)

**Invite someone** (name + an open question):
- **What do you think, Sari?** / **Sari, what's your view?**
- **We haven't heard from Dimas yet.** (*kita belum dengar pendapat Dimas*)

**Hand back:**
- **Sorry, go ahead.** (*maaf, silakan duluan*): when two people start at the same time.
- **Anyway, that's my view. What about you?**

id.text:
**Turn-taking** artinya siapa bicara kapan. Di sini budaya sama pentingnya dengan kata-katanya.

Di banyak **rapat di Indonesia**, orang menunggu orang yang paling senior (*Pak/Bu*, atasan) bicara dulu, dan yang junior bicara kalau ditanya. Itu tanda hormat.

Di banyak **kelompok berbahasa Inggris** (perusahaan internasional, seminar di luar negeri, panggilan dengan tim di luar negeri), harapannya berbeda: semua orang, termasuk yang junior, diharapkan **ikut bicara tanpa ditanya**, dan menyela sebentar dengan sopan saat ada jeda itu hal biasa. Kalau kamu diam saja, orang bisa mengira kamu tidak punya ide, atau kamu setuju.

Tidak ada gaya yang lebih baik: perhatikan saja mana yang diharapkan kelompoknya. Kamu bisa ikut bicara dan tetap sopan: tunggu jeda, pakai frasa yang lembut, sampaikan poinmu dengan singkat.

**Mengambil giliran:**
- **Can I come in here?** (*boleh saya ikut bicara?*)
- **Sorry to interrupt, but …** (*maaf menyela, tapi …*)
- **Can I just add something?** (*boleh saya menambahkan sesuatu?*)

**Mengajak seseorang** (nama + pertanyaan terbuka):
- **What do you think, Sari?** / **Sari, what's your view?**
- **We haven't heard from Dimas yet.** (*kita belum dengar pendapat Dimas*)

**Mengembalikan giliran:**
- **Sorry, go ahead.** (*maaf, silakan duluan*): kalau dua orang mulai bicara bersamaan.
- **Anyway, that's my view. What about you?**

blocks.text:
Inviting a quiet colleague: use their **name** + an **open question** (one that can't be answered with just *yes*). Don't say *Why are you so quiet?* or *Say something!*: it puts them on the spot (*bikin malu*). And if you're the senior person, try asking the juniors first: in an Indonesian team, they may be waiting for you.
**Can I come in here?** has nothing to do with a room: it means *may I join the conversation now?*

id.text:
Mengajak rekan yang pendiam: pakai **namanya** + **pertanyaan terbuka** (yang tidak bisa dijawab hanya dengan *yes*). Jangan bilang *Why are you so quiet?* atau *Say something!*: itu bikin dia malu di depan semua orang. Dan kalau kamu yang paling senior, coba tanya yang junior dulu: di tim Indonesia, mereka mungkin sedang menunggumu.
**Can I come in here?** tidak ada hubungannya dengan ruangan: artinya *boleh saya ikut bicara sekarang?*

blocks.prompt: You and Rina start speaking at exactly the same time. What's a polite thing to say?
blocks.explain: **Sorry, go ahead.** lets Rina speak first; you can take your turn after her. The other two sound rude in a discussion.

id.prompt: Kamu dan Rina mulai bicara tepat bersamaan. Apa yang sopan untuk dikatakan?
id.explain: **Sorry, go ahead.** mempersilakan Rina bicara dulu; kamu bisa mengambil giliran setelahnya. Dua pilihan lainnya terdengar kasar dalam diskusi.

blocks.text: Pak Hasan's team is discussing an idea: letting staff work from anywhere (Bali, Yogyakarta, their hometown) for one month a year. Find how they **invite** people, **buy time**, **take a turn**, **build on** each other, weigh **pros and cons** and **speculate**.

id.text: Tim Pak Hasan sedang mendiskusikan sebuah ide: membolehkan karyawan bekerja dari mana saja (Bali, Yogyakarta, kampung halaman) selama satu bulan setahun. Temukan bagaimana mereka **mengajak** orang bicara, **mengulur waktu**, **mengambil giliran**, **melanjutkan** poin satu sama lain, menimbang **kelebihan dan kekurangan** dan **berspekulasi**.

rows.en: Pak Hasan: So, should we let people work from anywhere for a month? Rina, what do you think?
rows.id: Pak Hasan: Jadi, apakah kita sebaiknya membolehkan orang bekerja dari mana saja selama sebulan? Rina, bagaimana menurutmu?

rows.en: Rina: Hmm, that's a good question. On the plus side, people could come back with more energy.
rows.id: Rina: Hmm, pertanyaan bagus. Sisi positifnya, orang-orang bisa kembali dengan lebih semangat.

rows.en: Budi: Can I come in here? The downside is that the internet isn't always good outside big cities.
rows.id: Budi: Boleh saya ikut bicara? Kekurangannya adalah internet tidak selalu bagus di luar kota besar.

rows.en: Sari: Following on from what Budi said, it could be that we need some clear rules first.
rows.id: Sari: Melanjutkan apa yang Budi bilang, bisa jadi kita butuh beberapa aturan yang jelas dulu.

rows.en: Pak Hasan: Good point. We haven't heard from Dimas yet. Dimas?
rows.id: Pak Hasan: Poin bagus. Kita belum dengar pendapat Dimas. Dimas?

rows.en: Dimas: I'd imagine most people are interested. On balance, I think it's worth a try.
rows.id: Dimas: Saya kira kebanyakan orang tertarik. Setelah menimbang semuanya, menurut saya ini layak dicoba.

blocks.prompt: In the discussion, how does Pak Hasan make sure everyone speaks?
options: He invites people by name with an open question.
He asks Dimas why he's so quiet.
blocks.explain: Pak Hasan says **Rina, what do you think?** and **We haven't heard from Dimas yet. Dimas?**: a name plus an open invitation. He doesn't wait, and he doesn't put Dimas on the spot.

id.prompt: Dalam diskusi itu, bagaimana Pak Hasan memastikan semua orang bicara?
id.explain: Pak Hasan bilang **Rina, what do you think?** dan **We haven't heard from Dimas yet. Dimas?**: nama ditambah ajakan terbuka. Dia tidak menunggu, dan tidak membuat Dimas malu.
options: Dia mengajak orang dengan menyebut nama dan pertanyaan terbuka.
Dia bertanya mengapa Dimas sangat pendiam.

suggestedQuestions: How can I join a discussion when everyone talks fast?
Is it rude to interrupt in an English meeting?
What's the difference between I suspect and I'd imagine?
How do I disagree with my boss in a discussion?

resources.title: Discussing advantages and disadvantages (B2 speaking)

With the phrases explained, the transcript and practice tasks. It adds a few extra phrases (On the one hand … on the other hand, I see where you're coming from).

Dengan penjelasan frasa, transkrip dan latihan. Ada beberapa frasa tambahan (On the one hand … on the other hand, I see where you're coming from).

resources.title: Conversation Skills: Interrupting politely in English
resources.note: A video lesson, all in English, on when it's OK to interrupt and how to do it politely, what to say when someone interrupts you, and body language that shows you'd like a turn. It teaches extra phrases beyond this lesson (Can I just mention something?).

id.note: Video pelajaran, seluruhnya dalam bahasa Inggris, tentang kapan boleh menyela dan cara melakukannya dengan sopan, apa yang dikatakan kalau ada yang menyelamu, dan bahasa tubuh yang menunjukkan kamu ingin giliran bicara. Ada frasa tambahan di luar pelajaran ini (Can I just mention something?).

id.intro: Dalam diskusi sungguhan, tidak ada yang memberimu waktu untuk bersiap. Di pelajaran ini kamu akan belajar ikut bicara dengan wajar: mengulur waktu beberapa detik untuk berpikir, melanjutkan apa yang dikatakan orang lain, menimbang kelebihan dan kekurangan, menebak dengan hati-hati, dan bergiliran bicara tanpa menunggu ditanya. Pemanasan: apakah perusahaan sebaiknya membolehkan karyawan bekerja dari mana saja selama sebulan setahun?
suggestedQuestions: Bagaimana cara ikut diskusi kalau semua orang bicara cepat?
Apakah menyela itu tidak sopan di rapat berbahasa Inggris?
Apa bedanya I suspect dan I'd imagine?
Bagaimana cara tidak setuju dengan atasan dalam diskusi?

assessment.ds-1: Di wawancara kerja di Jakarta, manajer menanyakan sesuatu yang tidak kamu duga: 'How will AI change our industry in the next five years?' Kamu butuh beberapa detik untuk berpikir. Tulis frasa pendek (2–6 kata) dalam bahasa Inggris untuk mengulur waktu sebelum menjawab.
assessment.ds-2: Di sebuah seminar, Dimas bilang kelas online menghemat uang mahasiswa. Kamu setuju dan ingin melanjutkan poinnya. Lengkapi dengan satu kata: Following ___ from what Dimas said, students also don't have to pay for a kos near campus.
assessment.ds-3: Rina dapat tawaran kerja di Singapura. Dia menimbangnya: 'On the plus side, the salary is much higher. The ___ is that I'll be far from my family.' Lengkapi dengan satu kata.
assessment.ds-4: Temanmu bertanya: 'Will the office trip to Puncak happen on Saturday?' Perbaiki kesalahan dalam balasan ini: It's depend on the weather.
assessment.ds-5: Timmu mengirim email penting ke klien seminggu lalu, dan masih belum ada balasan. Tidak ada yang tahu kenapa. Buat tebakan yang hati-hati. Lengkapi dengan satu kata: It ___ be that they're on holiday.
assessment.ds-6: Di rapat, Pak Hasan sedang membicarakan anggaran baru. Kamu punya poin penting soal itu, dan dia berhenti sebentar. Lengkapi frasa sopan untuk mengambil giliran dengan satu kata: Can I come ___ here?
assessment.ds-7: Kamu memimpin rapat online. Sari belum bicara sama sekali, dan kamu ingin mendengar idenya. Tulis pertanyaan pendek (2–6 kata) dalam bahasa Inggris untuk mengajaknya bicara.
